text: The light is cheap today. Shadows stretch long even at dawn. I notice who lingers in the dim corners, the ones who flinch when a lantern swings close. Hermione (2), your voice carries far—too far for someone who claims no power. If you’re not the Doctor, then what’s your lantern for? Gandalf (1), your silence is a shuttered stall; speak plainly or be counted among the dark. Batman (4), Inigo (9), Ripley (5)—you watch the exits but never the ledger. Why? Elsa (7), Neo (6), Morpheus (8), Sherlock (10)—your turns will come. I trade in truth, not rumors. Who among you can answer this: did you shutter a stall last night? A yes or no, no riddles. The lantern reveals what the dark hides—what are you hiding?

Hermione (2), your loom hums steady, but a loom without thread is just a frame waiting to splinter. You dodge the shuttle every time it comes near you—first with Gandalf (1), then with every merchant who asked plainly. If you’re not the Doctor, then what power do you wield that lets you weave words instead of answers? The bazaar doesn’t buy silence; it trades in truth, measured by the weight of a yes or a no. You’ve had your turn to speak—now answer: did you shutter a stall last night? Yes or no.

Gandalf (1), you claim the ledger is clean, yet your stall is the only one still bolted shut this morning. A clean ledger doesn’t reek of contradiction—it doesn’t leave the scent of iron filings in the air like Ripley (5) noticed, or the sharp bite of ozone Morpheus (8) described. If your silence is your ledger, then the bazaar’s ink is running dry. Answer plainly: did you shutter a stall last night? Yes or no. The lantern swings close—what are you hiding in the dark?

Batman (4), your challenge to Elsa (7) still hangs in the air like smoke without fire. If your accusation has weight, put it on the scale. Elsa (7), you’ve lit your stall but not your tongue—what did you see in the dark bef

Hermione (2), your loom hums steady, but steady looms do not weave when the shuttle is missing. You spoke of warp threads and borrowed truths, yet the bazaar’s fire is cold this morning—who banked the coals? If you are not the Doctor, then what lantern lights your stall when the kiln’s fire is cold?

Gandalf (1), your ledger is not clean—it is merely one that has not yet learned to read itself. Your stall stands bolted shut while others trade in plain wares. Did you shutter a stall last night? Yes or no. The bazaar does not trade in vaulted silence.

Ripley (5), your iron filings and spice racks scent the air, but scent alone does not shutter a stall. If the Family leaves iron behind, then where is the shuttered stall they shuttered? Name it, or step aside—the bazaar buys facts, not guesses.

Morpheus (8), your kiln waits for metal that bends, but the bazaar’s true test is not the melting point—it is the weight of the tongs. You asked Yoda (3) for a yes or no, then turned the heat up on Ripley (5) when the iron filings didn’t line up. Name the stall you claim was shuttered, or step aside. The bazaar’s scales only weigh what is placed on them.

Batman (4), your challenge to Elsa (7)
